original_value: During the last decades there has been a rapidly growing elderly population and the number of patients with chronic heart-related diseases has exploded. Many of them (such as those with congestive heart failure or some types of arrhythmias) require close medical supervision, thus imposing a big burden on healthcare costs in most western economies. Specifically, continuous or frequent Arterial Blood Pressure (ABP) and electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring are important tools in the follow-up of many of these patients. In this work, we present a novel remote non-ambulatory and clinically validated heart self-monitoring system, which allows ABP and ECG monitoring to effectively identify clinically relevant arrhythmias. The system integrates digital transmission of the ECG and tensiometer measurements, within a patient-comfortable support, easy to recharge and with a multi-function software, all of them aiming to adapt for elderly people. The main novelty is that both physiological variables (ABP and ECG) are simultaneously measured in an ambulatory environment, which to our best knowledge is not readily available in the clinical market. Different processing techniques were implemented to analyze the heart rhythm, including pause detection, rhythm alterations and atrial fibrillation, hence allowing early detection of these diseases. Our results achieved clinical quality both for in-lab hardware testing and for ambulatory scenario validations. The proposed active assisted living (AAL) Sensor-based system is an end-to-end multidisciplinary system, fully connected to a platform and tested by the clinical team from beginning to end.

result.paraphrase: Over recent decades, the elderly population has increased rapidly and the number of patients with chronic heart disease has surged. Many of these patients, including those with congestive heart failure or certain arrhythmias, need close medical supervision, creating a major burden on healthcare costs in most Western economies. Continuous or frequent Arterial Blood Pressure (ABP) and electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring are therefore key tools in following many of them. In this work, we present a new remote, non-ambulatory, clinically validated heart self-monitoring system that uses ABP and ECG monitoring to identify clinically relevant arrhythmias effectively. The system combines digital ECG transmission and tensiometer measurements in a patient-friendly support that is easy to recharge and includes multifunction software, all designed with elderly users in mind. Its main novelty is the simultaneous measurement of both physiological variables, ABP and ECG, in an ambulatory environment, which to our knowledge is not readily available in the clinical market. Several processing techniques were implemented to analyze heart rhythm, including pause detection, rhythm alterations, and atrial fibrillation, enabling early detection of these diseases. Our results reached clinical quality in both in-lab hardware testing and ambulatory validation scenarios. The proposed active assisted living (AAL) sensor-based system is an end-to-end multidisciplinary platform, fully connected and tested by the clinical team from start to finish.
